intended_object: A mixin class saying that addition on an additive monoid that is also a (pseudo)metric space is jointly Lipschitz: there is a constant C ≥ 0 such that (x, y) ↦ x + y is C-Lipschitz on β × β, with the product (sup) metric. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body requires `∃ C : ℝ≥0, LipschitzWith C (fun p : β × β => p.1 + p.2)`. On β × β, `LipschitzWith` is taken with respect to the product (sup) extended distance. So the class says exactly that addition is jointly Lipschitz, which matches the docstring. It is the additive counterpart of `LipschitzMul`, written out by hand just above `LipschitzMul`'s `@[to_additive]`. The module documentation says these classes are meant to cover what normed groups and ℝ≥0 have in common.

The `AddMonoid` assumption is a little stronger than needed: the statement only uses `+`, so `[Add β]` would be enough. Still, the class is meant for monoids. Its multiplicative twin uses `[Monoid β]`, and the library code built on it (submonoid instances, the Lipschitz constant `LipschitzMul.C`) works with monoid structure. This mismatch is too minor to make the definition too narrow.

Degenerate cases cause no problems: C may be 0, and empty or trivial types are handled correctly.
